authorities.title: Equity
supports: Florida mortgages are foreclosed in equity; mortgage foreclosure is a court proceeding rather than California-style nonjudicial trustee-sale procedure.

authorities.title: Elements of complaint; lost, destroyed, or stolen note affidavit
supports: Covered residential foreclosure complaints must contain specified allegations concerning plaintiff status and note enforcement, with additional requirements when the note is lost, destroyed, or stolen.

authorities.title: Power to set aside foreclosure decrees before sale
supports: Florida law recognizes judicial authority under the statute to set aside a foreclosure decree before the foreclosure sale; this is not an unconditional homeowner right to cancel a sale.

authorities.title: Order to show cause; entry of final judgment of foreclosure; payment during foreclosure
supports: Section 702.10 creates distinct show-cause procedures. For final-judgment show cause, the hearing timing depends on statutory service-related conditions rather than the ordinary complaint-answer clock; subsection (2) creates a separate payment/vacate show-cause track and excludes owner-occupied residential real estate from that subsection.

authorities.title: Defenses — time to serve answer
supports: Current Rule 1.140(a)(1), updated through April 1, 2026, requires a defendant to serve an answer within 20 days after service of original process and the initial pleading unless a Florida statute prescribes a different time.

authorities.citation: Fla. R. Gen. Prac. & Jud. Admin. 2.514
authorities.title: Computing and Extending Time
supports: Current Rule 2.514, updated July 1, 2026, supplies the statewide computation method for procedural, local-rule, court-order, or statutory periods that do not specify their own method; it separately addresses periods under 7 days and periods of 7 days or longer.

authorities.title: Summary Judgment
supports: Current Rule 1.510, as compiled through April 1, 2026 and reflecting amendments effective January 1, 2025, requires a response no later than 40 days after service of the summary-judgment motion and requires the hearing to be set at least 10 days after the response deadline, subject to stipulation, court order, and case-management deadlines.

authorities.title: Judicial sales procedure
supports: When the court orders use of §45.031, judicial sale, certificate of sale, sale objections, certificate of title, confirmation, and title passage are distinct events; objections to sale are filed within 10 days after filing of the certificate of sale, and if no objections are filed the clerk files the certificate of title, upon which the sale is confirmed and title passes.

authorities.title: Right of redemption
supports: The mortgagor or subordinate-interest holder may redeem before the later of filing of the certificate of sale or the time specified in the foreclosure judgment, order, or decree, subject to the statute's payment/tender requirements; this is an event-based cutoff rather than a generic fixed-days-after-sale rule.

authorities.title: Enforcement of Final Judgments — Property Recovery
supports: For a judgment recovering real property, final process is by writ of possession; this is distinct from a money execution and from the underlying foreclosure sale/title events.

authorities.title: Writ of Possession
supports: When a judgment or order is for delivery of possession of real property, the judgment or order directs the clerk to issue a writ of possession; the clerk issues the writ forthwith and delivers it to the sheriff for execution.

If a person other than the party against whom the writ issued is in possession, Rule 1.580(b) permits that person to file an affidavit with the sheriff claiming entitlement to possession; the sheriff then desists until the court determines whether execution should continue or be stayed.

authorities.title: Writ of Possession
supports: The current statewide writ form commands the county sheriff to remove persons from the described real property and put the named person in possession; the form itself does not publish a statewide foreclosure-specific posting countdown.

authorities.title: Final Judgment of Foreclosure
supports: The current standard foreclosure-judgment form treats filing of the certificate of title as the point at which the person named on that certificate is to be let into possession, subject to qualifying bona fide tenant rights under the federal PTFA and the form's referenced state provision.
The standard form preserves title/possession as distinct from certificate of sale and redemption events; the actual signed judgment controls in a specific case.

authorities.title: Stay Pending Review
supports: Except for specified exceptions, filing a notice of appeal does not itself stay enforcement; a party seeking a stay pending review generally first applies in the lower tribunal, which may grant, modify, deny, or condition a stay.

mortgage_default_letter.label: I RECEIVED A MORTGAGE DEFAULT / ACCELERATION LETTER
mortgage_default_letter.description: Pre-suit default and acceleration requirements may arise from the note/mortgage, servicer law, federal servicing rules, and loan program. No generic Florida pre-suit clock is inferred.
exceptions: The loan documents and federal servicing coverage matter; VA assistance or Regulation X does not automatically stop a Florida court foreclosure.

foreclosure_complaint.label: I WAS SERVED WITH A FORECLOSURE COMPLAINT
foreclosure_complaint.description: Florida mortgage foreclosure is a judicial action. For an ordinary foreclosure complaint, the current civil-rule answer clock is independent from Chapter 83's five-day eviction procedure.

immediate_clock.label: ordinary foreclosure answer period
immediate_clock.trigger: service of original process and the initial foreclosure pleading on the defendant
immediate_clock.display: Current Fla. R. Civ. P. 1.140(a)(1) generally requires an answer within 20 days after service of original process and the initial pleading unless a Florida statute prescribes a different time; compute the period under the governing Florida time rule and follow any controlling court order or case-specific paper.

exceptions: This is not the Chapter 83 eviction five-day response period.
A statute can prescribe a different time; actual summons, service, and court orders must be reviewed.
Complaint pleading requirements do not make every defect automatically case-dispositive.

order_to_show_cause.label: I RECEIVED AN ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE
order_to_show_cause.description: Section 702.10 is an expedited, court-controlled procedure separate from the ordinary Rule 1.140 answer deadline and separate from summary judgment. The final-judgment show-cause hearing uses statutory later-of timing tied to service; subsection (2) contains a separate payment/vacate track.
exceptions: No single generic countdown is published because the court-set hearing depends on the applicable subsection and service events.
Under §702.10(2), the payment/vacate show-cause procedure does not apply to owner-occupied residential real estate.
Failure to appear or respond can have serious consequences, but final judgment still depends on the statutory and court findings.

summary_judgment.label: A MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT WAS FILED
summary_judgment.description: Current Florida Rule 1.510 creates a separate response/hearing schedule for summary judgment. It is not the foreclosure complaint answer clock.

immediate_clock.label: summary-judgment response period
immediate_clock.trigger: service of the motion for summary judgment
immediate_clock.display: Under current Rule 1.510, a response to a summary-judgment motion is due no later than 40 days after service of the motion, subject to court-ordered case-management deadlines and the governing computation rule.

other_clocks.label: minimum hearing spacing after response deadline
other_clocks.trigger: deadline for serving the summary-judgment response
other_clocks.display: The summary-judgment hearing must be set at least 10 days after the response deadline, unless the parties stipulate or the court orders otherwise as permitted by the rule.

exceptions: The actual case-management order and hearing notice must be reviewed.
This route explains procedure; it does not prescribe individualized litigation strategy.

final_judgment.label: A FINAL JUDGMENT OF FORECLOSURE WAS ENTERED
final_judgment.description: A final judgment determines the foreclosure relief and may set sale terms, but judgment is not the sale, appeal is not an automatic stay, and redemption has its own statutory cutoff.
exceptions: Read the judgment for the property, adjudged amount, sale date, court, and any time the judgment expressly fixes for redemption.
Do not treat an appeal as automatically staying enforcement; stay issues require separate authority and case review.

judicial_sale.label: A FORECLOSURE SALE IS SCHEDULED / WAS CONDUCTED
judicial_sale.description: When §45.031 is used, the judicial sale is one event in a court-controlled chain. The sale is followed by a certificate-of-sale event and does not itself equal passage of title or physical removal.
exceptions: The final judgment and sale notice control the scheduled sale event; this route does not publish a generalized sale-scheduling countdown.
Sale, certificate of sale, objections, certificate of title, redemption, and possession remain distinct.

certificate_of_sale.label: A CERTIFICATE OF SALE WAS FILED
certificate_of_sale.description: After the judicial sale, the clerk promptly files a certificate of sale. Its filing date is a distinct legal event that triggers the statutory sale-objection period and is also one branch of Florida's event-based redemption cutoff.
exceptions: Record the actual filing date from the docket; do not substitute the auction date if different.

sale_objection.label: I NEED TO UNDERSTAND THE SALE-OBJECTION PERIOD
sale_objection.description: Section 45.031 ties objections to the filing of the certificate of sale—not simply to the auction time.

immediate_clock.label: objection to judicial sale
immediate_clock.trigger: filing of the certificate of sale by the clerk
immediate_clock.display: If §45.031 governs, objections to the sale are filed within 10 days after the clerk files the certificate of sale; use the certificate filing date and the governing Florida time-computation rule.

exceptions: An objection to sale is not an appeal and is not the statutory right of redemption.
The exact grounds and procedural vehicle are legal issues; this route does not give individualized objection strategy.

certificate_of_title.label: A CERTIFICATE OF TITLE WAS FILED
certificate_of_title.description: Under §45.031, filing of the certificate of title confirms the judicial sale and passes title to the purchaser. Current Form 1.996(a) separately provides that the person named on the certificate of title is to be let into possession, subject to qualifying bona fide-tenant rights. Title passage is not itself physical sheriff execution.
exceptions: The actual signed foreclosure judgment controls; Form 1.996(a) is the current statewide standard form, not a substitute for reading the judgment in the case.
A bona fide tenant can have federal PTFA rights that qualify the purchaser's right to possession.
Certificate of title, writ of possession, sheriff execution, and physical removal are separate events.

redemption.label: I NEED TO UNDERSTAND THE RIGHT OF REDEMPTION
redemption.description: Florida's right of redemption is event-based, not a generic number of days after sale. Under §45.0315 the cutoff is the later of filing of the certificate of sale or a different time specified in the foreclosure judgment, order, or decree, subject to the statutory payment/tender requirements.
exceptions: Redemption is not the same as objecting to sale, reinstatement, modification, payoff negotiations, appeal, or vacating a judgment.
Because the controlling cutoff can depend on the judgment/order, no fixed numeric clock is published.
Expiration of redemption rights does not itself equal a writ of possession or completed physical sheriff execution; redemption and possession are separate legal events.

post_sale_former_owner.label: I WAS THE BORROWER / OWNER AND THE CERTIFICATE OF TITLE WAS FILED
post_sale_former_owner.description: For a former mortgagor/owner, the post-title possession path is controlled by the foreclosure judgment/order and Florida's general real-property judgment-enforcement rules. When the judgment/order delivers possession, Rule 1.580 directs issuance of a writ of possession to the sheriff. The certificate of title is not itself a self-help lockout.
exceptions: Former owner status is not bona fide tenant status; do not apply PTFA merely because the former borrower remains physically in the property.
The actual final judgment/order must be reviewed to determine whether it delivers possession and what further court order, if any, is required.
No statewide foreclosure-specific posting countdown is published here because Rule 1.580 and Form 1.915 do not establish one.

post_sale_bona_fide_tenant.label: I AM A BONA FIDE TENANT IN THE FORECLOSED PROPERTY
post_sale_bona_fide_tenant.description: A qualifying bona fide tenant after foreclosure requires federal PTFA analysis before possession. Current Form 1.996(a) expressly makes the certificate-of-title holder's possession subject to bona fide tenant rights. If a tenant is a person other than the party against whom a writ issued, Rule 1.580(b) can also provide a state procedural mechanism to assert a possession claim to the sheriff pending court review.
exceptions: PTFA bona fide tenancy requires the federal statutory conditions; relationship to the former mortgagor, lease timing, and rent terms matter.
Do not apply the PTFA route to the former mortgagor merely because that person remains in possession.
Rule 1.580(b) applies only when the occupant is a person other than the party against whom the writ issued; actual party/writ status must be checked.
The federal PTFA 90-day protection and fixed-term lease rules remain in the federal overlay rather than being converted into a Florida foreclosure clock.

post_sale_other_occupant.label: I DO NOT KNOW MY OCCUPANT STATUS AFTER FORECLOSURE
post_sale_other_occupant.description: Unknown occupant status must be identified before a possession rule is applied. The first task is document and relationship classification, not assigning tenant or former-owner rights.
exceptions: Identify whether the occupant is named on a lease, the former owner/borrower, related to the former owner, paying rent, occupying under a written or oral agreement, or another category.
Record the lease date, rent amount, purchaser identity, certificate-of-title filing date, writ details, and whether the occupant was a party to the foreclosure.
Unknown status must remain unknown; do not default to tenant, bona fide tenant, or former-owner treatment.

post_sale_writ_of_possession.label: I RECEIVED / FOUND A WRIT OF POSSESSION AFTER FORECLOSURE
post_sale_writ_of_possession.description: A foreclosure possession writ is a post-judgment enforcement document. Under Rules 1.570 and 1.580, a judgment/order delivering real-property possession is enforced by a writ of possession that the clerk issues and delivers to the sheriff for execution. This route does not import Chapter 83's residential-eviction 24-hour clock.
exceptions: The actual judgment/order and writ control; verify who the writ is issued against and who is physically occupying the property.

If a person other than the party against whom the writ issued is in possession and claims a right to possession, Rule 1.580(b) provides an affidavit-to-the-sheriff process that can halt execution while the court determines possession.
No statewide foreclosure-specific 24-hour posting rule is established by Rule 1.580 or Form 1.915.

post_sale_sheriff_execution.label: THE SHERIFF IS EXECUTING A FORECLOSURE WRIT OF POSSESSION
post_sale_sheriff_execution.description: Physical removal occurs through sheriff execution of the writ, not merely because a foreclosure sale or certificate of title occurred. Statewide Rule 1.580 identifies the sheriff as the executing officer but does not publish a universal foreclosure-specific posting or waiting period; county operational practice must remain local.
exceptions: Do not reuse §83.62's landlord-tenant 24-hour writ rule unless controlling authority independently makes that statute applicable to the particular foreclosure-possession track.
County sheriff scheduling, intake, and operational timing are local guidance and are not statewide legal deadlines.
A qualifying third-party occupant may fall within Rule 1.580(b)'s affidavit procedure.

post_sale_other_tenant.label: I AM A TENANT BUT I MAY NOT QUALIFY AS A PTFA BONA FIDE TENANT
post_sale_other_tenant.description: Failure to satisfy the federal PTFA definition does not by itself establish that an occupant has no rights. The lease, party status in the foreclosure, priority or survival of the tenancy, judgment language, and any other housing-program overlay must be identified before a possession conclusion is rendered.
exceptions: Not PTFA-qualified is not equivalent to no protection.
Do not automatically reuse ordinary landlord-tenant termination rules without first identifying whether the tenancy survived or was foreclosed and what the judgment provides.
If the occupant is not the party against whom the writ issued, Rule 1.580(b) may be relevant; actual party status matters.

appeal_stay_postsale.label: I FILED / AM CONSIDERING AN APPEAL AND POSSESSION IS MOVING FORWARD
appeal_stay_postsale.description: For a foreclosure judgment or post-sale possession order, filing an appeal generally does not itself create a stay. Current Rule 9.310 provides the stay-pending-review framework and generally requires a stay request in the lower tribunal unless an exception applies.
exceptions: Appeal and stay are separate procedural events.
Whether a stay exists depends on an entered stay, applicable exception, bond/conditions, and the actual order; this route does not provide individualized appellate strategy.
Document-first review should ask whether a notice of appeal was filed, whether a stay order exists, whether the sale already occurred, whether title issued, and whether a writ issued.

post_sale_document_router.label: FORECLOSURE SALE / TITLE / POSSESSION PAPERS — IDENTIFY MY DOCUMENT
post_sale_document_router.description: Post-sale routing is document-driven. Sale, certificate of sale, certificate of title, writ of possession, sheriff execution, and occupant-status questions are distinct legal events and must route separately.
exceptions: A foreclosure sale is not a certificate of sale.
A certificate of sale is not a certificate of title.
A certificate of title is not a writ of possession.
A writ of possession is not completed physical sheriff execution.
Redemption expiration and sale-objection expiration are not possession deadlines.

florida_bar_lrs.name: The Florida Bar Lawyer Referral Service
florida_bar_lrs.note: Referral service; representation and fees are not guaranteed.

florida_legal_aid.name: Florida Courts Legal Aid Locator
florida_legal_aid.note: Statewide legal-aid locator; eligibility and representation vary.

fdva.name: Florida Department of Veterans' Affairs
fdva.note: Veteran benefits/service routing; does not override foreclosure procedure.

fdva_county_vso.name: Florida County Veteran Service Officer Locator
fdva_county_vso.note: County VSO routing; not foreclosure representation.

hud_housing_counseling.name: HUD-Approved Housing Counselor Locator
hud_housing_counseling.note: Housing counseling; not court representation or an automatic stay.

va_lsv_h.name: VA Legal Services for Veterans (LSV-H)
va_lsv_h.note: Current grantee routing for eligible veterans experiencing or at risk of homelessness; representation and service availability are not guaranteed.

va_ssvf.name: VA Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF)
va_ssvf.note: Homelessness-prevention/rapid-rehousing provider routing; not a legal defense or entitlement.

va_home_loan.name: VA Help to Avoid Foreclosure / Loan Technician Assistance
va_home_loan.note: VA-backed loans are generally privately owned/serviced with a VA guaranty. VA assistance is not an automatic Florida foreclosure stay.
